description: Given a 2D integer array matrix, return the transpose of matrix. The transpose flips a matrix over its main diagonal, switching the row and column indices.
intuition: Transposing a matrix simply means swapping rows and columns. The element at row i, column j moves to row j, column i. Think of it as flipping the matrix along its main diagonal.
approach: Create a new matrix where element at position [i][j] comes from the original matrix at position [j][i]. The new matrix has dimensions cols x rows.
jsWalkthrough:
Example: matrix = [[1,2,3],[4,5,6],[7,8,9]]
rows=3, cols=3

i=0 (new row 0): collect column 0 of original
  j=0: matrix[0][0]=1, j=1: matrix[1][0]=4, j=2: matrix[2][0]=7
  result[0] = [1,4,7]
i=1 (new row 1): collect column 1 of original
  result[1] = [2,5,8]
i=2 (new row 2): collect column 2 of original
  result[2] = [3,6,9]
Result: [[1,4,7],[2,5,8],[3,6,9]]
explanation:
1. The original matrix has dimensions rows x cols.
2. The transposed matrix has dimensions cols x rows.
3. For each position (i, j) in the transposed matrix, the value is matrix[j][i].
4. Use list comprehension to build the result.
hints: The transpose swaps rows and columns.
Element at [i][j] in the transpose is element [j][i] in the original.
The output dimensions are the reverse of the input dimensions.

phases.label: Copy every cell to its transposed position

timeComplexityBreakdown.note: Each of the m × n cells is read and written once.
